fact: ForeverLawn, a turf maker, says other companies often lay turf over dirt or concrete, or over a single layer of stone, which it says produces lackluster drainage, and that it builds a layered stone base instead.
quote: We use a multi-part base system, using different types of stone to create a layered base that will hold up to foot traffic, but not inhibit drainage. Oftentimes other turf companies will lay turf over dirt or concrete, or at most one layer of aggregate stone, producing lackluster drainage performance.
source_label: ForeverLawn, FAQs (What makes ForeverLawn's base installation system superior?)
notes: A maker's marketing FAQ, read with curl on 2026-09-25. It stands opposite SYNLawn's DIY guide (artificial-turf-nails-vs-staples.synlawn-glue-over-concrete), which allows a glue-down on concrete with no base; the page presents both.

fact: FieldTurf Landscape says a foam pad smooths small dips and bumps in the surface under it, compensating for unevenness up to about 1/2 inch in height.
quote: Small dips, bumps, rocks, and inconsistencies in the base get smoothed out by the foam layer underneath. This allows for a flatter, more even installation over mildly irregular surfaces. The foam compensates for inconsistencies up to around 1/2″ in height.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, Foam Padding for Artificial Turf: Benefits, Uses & Safety
notes: Read from the raw HTML with curl on 2026-09-25. The same page's pooling-on-concrete sentence is does-artificial-turf-get-moldy.fieldturf-pad-moisture. The page is revised from time to time, hence the recheck.

fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse's installer column says outdoor glue-downs on concrete need more attention than indoor ones because temperature swings can make or break them, that adhesive bonds less well when the concrete is above 160 degrees, and recommends gluing early in the morning or early in the evening.
quote: Exterior “Glue Down” applications require more attention than Interior “Glue Down” applications. The temperature change alone can make or break an install. The concretes surface can reach up to blistering high degrees. Adhering Synthetic turf to concrete that is above 160 degrees lessens the penetration of both the adhesive to the concretes surface and the adhesion to the backing of the synthetic turf. I recommend installing the SGW Superseam Pro adhesive early in the morning or early evening when the temperature are cooler.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Gluing Synthetic Turf on Concrete (Aug. 2016)
notes: A turf supplier's installer column (datePublished 2016-08-24, dateModified 2022-12-29 in the page's structured data), read with curl on 2026-09-25. It names the supplier's own adhesive; the guide does not.

fact: The same column says the outside edges are the first part of a glue-down to fail, and that when a failed glue-down has to come up, removing the old adhesive before reinstalling can take days.
quote: Adhering synthetic turf to concrete isn’t as easy as it looks. I have watched contractors having to pulling up entire sections of indoor glue down applications due to poor installation and not understanding the process. This can be an expensive repair. The removal of the existing adhesive can take days to remove to get the surface ready for reinstalling. … When adhering synthetic turf on concrete it is very important to give attention to the outside edge line. The exterior edges are the first to fail when it comes to synthetic turf “Glue downs”.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Gluing Synthetic Turf on Concrete (Aug. 2016)
notes: The days-long adhesive removal is said of failed indoor glue-downs; the page says 'a failed glue-down', not 'an outdoor patio'.

fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse's installer column describes a dog-boarding yard where turf tiles on a thin plastic frame with 1/4-inch dimples sat on nearly flat asphalt, so waste collected as a slurry under the turf and never left, and the fix was to slope the whole area to a channel drain.
quote: The surface of the fenced areas was tiles of synthetic turf adhered on a thin plastic frame with ¼” dimples. These turf tiles, as I would call them, did not have enough elevation above the asphalt’s surface, which caused the dog feces to end up in a “slurry”. This slurry rested upon the asphalt and never exited the area. I noticed that the existing asphalt didn’t have much slope to it … I recommended that she slope the entire area back toward the building and into a channel drain.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Commercial Pet Area Installation Over Concrete (April 2021)
notes: A turf supplier's installer column (datePublished 2021-04-21), read with curl on 2026-09-25. A commercial kennel on asphalt, used on the page only to show what happens when a hard surface has no fall; the column promotes the supplier's drainage grid and infill, which the guide does not name.

fact: The same column fastens turf over concrete to a plastic board laid flat and anchored to the slab, cuts channels through the board every 3 to 6 inches so water can escape from under the turf, says boards on rooftops and balconies must be glued rather than drilled or nailed because drilling can make the surface leak, warns installers to respect wind lift, and says turf over concrete must be ballasted with infill because thermal expansion and contraction move it into wrinkles.
quote: When all the exterior nailer boards are cut into place, now is the time to cut openings for the escape of water and fluids if needed. … I recommend placing channels/holes at 3 to 6 inches on center to allow water and fluids to escape out and from under the installation. … You cannot drill or nail nailer boards to rooftops, balconies, and mezzanine surfaces. This will damage the surface and may cause the surface to leak below. … Remember, the system will not be completely secure until infill placement is completed. Respect wind lift in all areas. … When securing nailer boards flat on concrete or asphalt, I recommend drilling and securing with a tapered head concrete anchor or Red Head. … It is so important to ballast synthetic turf when it is placed on AirDrain, especially over concrete. The turf will move due to thermal expansion and contraction. When this happens, wrinkles will appear.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Commercial Pet Area Installation Over Concrete (April 2021)
notes: Same article as sgw-pet-slab-slurry. 'Red Head' is an anchor brand; the guide says 'concrete anchors'.

fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse's installer column strongly recommends a drainage grid under pet areas, rooftops, balconies and playgrounds, and says the grid it sells lifts turf about 1 inch so air and water move underneath.
quote: It is strongly recommended that a drainage grid be placed under Pet Relief Areas, Rooftops, Balconies and Playgrounds where aeration and permeation is needed. AirDrain is a low cost, easy to install, Geocell drainage grid that creates a 1 inch 92% air void underneath your artificial turf. AirDrain elevates the synthetic turf above the subgrade to allow air to circulate and water to pass through rapidly.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: What Drains Better Than Air? AirDrain Does (Nov. 2017)
notes: A supplier's column promoting a grid it sells (datePublished 2017-11-14), read with curl on 2026-09-25. The guide names the kind of product, never the brand.

fact: The same column describes a putting green raised so its edge near the house sat higher than the patio door's threshold, which let water flood the house, and tells installers not to take on responsibility for floodwater where a backyard sits higher than the foundation.
quote: Prior to installing any turf in a backyard that’s rear elevation is higher than the foundation of the home or building, it is imperative that you not take on the responsibility of floodwaters. … Raising of the putting greens edge near the house caused the entire length of the putting green to be much higher than the threshold of the patio door. This caused flooding to the interior.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: What Drains Better Than Air? AirDrain Does (Nov. 2017)
notes: A putting green, not a slab overlay; the guide uses it only for the door-threshold point.

fact: K9Grass's specification for indoor dog turf calls for a smooth, sloped, sealed floor that carries liquid waste to a drain, covered by a grid that raises the turf at least 1 inch so liquid can drain down and flow to the drain.
quote: Base is to be smooth, sloped, and sealed impermeable surface that directs liquid waste to an exit point (drain). … Base is to be covered with grid elevation system that raises floor surface a minimum of 1” and reduces contact with the floor to allow liquids to drain vertically as well as flow to drain.
source_label: K9Grass (ForeverLawn), Dog Specific Synthetic Grass Indoor Surface Specifications: K9Grass Endura (M1265 Rev. 7/24)
notes: Downloaded and read with pdftotext on 2026-09-25 (section 2, Base and Attaching Components). An indoor commercial spec; the guide uses it only to show what one maker asks of a slab under dog turf.

fact: SP-14 says cracks in slabs and outdoor flatwork should be monitored by measuring certain cracks every month and noting whether they stay the same, keep widening, or open and close with the seasons.
quote: Cracks in walls, floor slabs, and exterior flatwork should be monitored over time. This can be done by measuring the width of certain cracks every month and noting if the cracks stay the same, steadily increase in size over time, or expand and contract with the seasons.
source_label: Colorado Geological Survey SP-14, Home Landscaping and Maintenance on Swelling Soil (Jochim, 1981; revised fifth printing 1987)
notes: Read from the CGS-hosted PDF with pdftotext on 2026-09-25 (Appendix B, the house checklist). The flatwork-uplift, crack-and-tilt, patio-slope and backfill sentences from the same PDF are artificial-turf-vs-pavers-concrete records, cited by id.

fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse's installer column calls crushed recycled concrete a good base under landscape turf because it compacts well and drains, but advises against it under pet areas because the cement fines bonded to it can be very absorbent.
quote: Crushed recycled concrete is great for placing under landscape synthetic turf. It compacts well, provides great drainage, and gives long-term stability. … I do not recommend placing recycled crushed concrete under pet installations. … When concrete is recycled and broken up, fine sand, cement, and other particles remain intact, bonded to the aggregates. These bonded materials can be very absorbent.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Recycled Concrete & Synthetic Turf (Aug. 2021)
notes: A turf supplier's installer column (datePublished 2021-08-26), read with curl on 2026-09-25. The column goes on to say the absorbed urine may cause odors; the guide keeps to the absorbency point.
